items.title: Study reveals peatlands may have less capacity to store carbon than predicted
items.summary: A new study has revealed that peatlands may break under their own weight before they reach their carbon storage potential.

items.title: RNA 'delivery tags' guide key messages to distant neuron branches
items.summary: Much like a courier reading an address on a package, neurons must deliver RNA to the precise locations where it is needed. A KAIST research team has discovered how a small chemical modification on RNA acts as a "delivery tag," helping selected RNAs travel to distant regions of neurons.

items.title: Inspiration alone won't solve Australia's teacher shortage, study reveals
items.summary: A $10 million Australian government campaign celebrating inspirational teachers risked overlooking the workplace conditions driving educators from the profession, according to new research led by Curtin University published in the Journal of Education Policy.

items.title: Starfish program creates new jobs
items.summary: In a win for people and the environment, new economic modeling from James Cook University researchers reveals that a $5 million investment to control crown-of-thorns (CoTS) starfish numbers in the Cairns region created 61 new jobs and generated $20 million in economic activity.

items.title: Micro-dramas and the battle for attention
items.summary: As tech companies like Meta, Google and TikTok face ongoing scrutiny over addictive platform design, the rapid rise of micro-dramas offers a glimpse into how AI, algorithms and commercial incentives could make digital entertainment even harder to put down.

items.title: Gravitational-wave analysis narrows the search for black hole impostors
items.summary: Black holes are regions of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape. When two black holes orbit each other and merge, they produce gravitational waves (i.e., ripples in spacetime) that can resemble those emitted by mergers involving other exotic compact objects.

items.title: Fish may be highly sensitive to antidepressants found in water
items.summary: Many of the drugs that target human brain chemistry, such as antidepressants, are still biologically active when they leave the body. These substances and their metabolites can persist in wastewater and eventually end up in the sea, rivers or other aquatic environments.

items.title: Cataract surgery will be needed in space, surgeon predicts
items.summary: An eye surgeon with a passion for space since childhood predicts that as astronauts start to make journeys to the moon and Mars in the near future, eye surgery in space will eventually become a necessity.
